chunks: Saad narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal from Amr ibn Sa'id al-Mad'ani from Musaddiq ibn Sadah from Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who is fasting and has intercourse with his wife, so he said, 'He performs ghusl and there is nothing upon him.' This report is understood to mean that if he had intercourse unintentionally and not deliberately, then nothing is required of him, and the state is as we described. It also carries the possibility that the intended meaning is one who does not know that this is not permissible for him in the Sharia. What indicates this is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a fasting person who has intercourse with their spouse?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a fasting man who has intercourse with his wife is only required to perform *ghusl* without incurring the major expiation (*kaffarah*), provided the act was not deliberate. Shia jurists interpret this ruling as applying either to those who acted out of forgetfulness (*nasi*) or to those who were genuinely ignorant of the prohibition (*jahil*), thereby distinguishing these cases from the deliberate breaker of fast who must offer the full expiation.
